sources: West Point, Calaveras County: California Historical Landmark No. 268, registered 9/3/1937, at the intersection of State Hwy 26 (P.M. 34.4) and Main St. Plaque text: named by Kit Carson while searching for a pass over the Sierra; a thriving trading post before the gold discovery; one emigrant road forked at Big Meadows and its north branch came directly to West Point. No year is given for Carson: https://ohp.parks.ca.gov/ListedResources/Detail/268
The plaque was placed by the California Centennials Commission, base by the Mokelumne Lions Club, dedicated July 3, 1949 (plaque transcription, noehill.com): https://noehill.com/calaveras/cal0268.asp
Carson's search for a pass is commonly dated to the 1844 Fremont expedition. That year is TRADITION, not stated on the plaque or the OHP record.
West Point was established as a mining supply camp by 1854; early emigration came from Volcano across the Mokelumne River (Calaveras Heritage Council): https://www.calaverashistory.org/west-point

Sandy Gulch: an 1849 trading center for miners, named for the gulch where William and Dan Carsner found nuggets in coarse sand; quartz mining began in the early 1850s. The monument is on State Hwy 26 (P.M. 32.3), 2.1 mi from West Point toward Glencoe, which is about 2.3 km SSW in a straight line, not in this camp (California OHP, Landmark No. 253): https://ohp.parks.ca.gov/ListedResources/Detail/253
Willows on Main, the general store front and the Main Street boardwalk are later explore attractions (period 'later'). The dates of those buildings are not sourced here.

later_sites.label: General store
later_sites.notYet: No store front yet. The plaque records a trading post here before the gold; what it looked like is not known.

later_sites.label: Kit Carson marker
later_sites.notYet: Hwy 26 & Main. Registered in 1937, the plaque dedicated in 1949. Carson's search for a pass is by tradition 1844.

later_sites.label: Sandy Gulch Mine
later_sites.notYet: Not here: Sandy Gulch is 2 miles down the road, south-southwest. The gulch is already being worked; the quartz mills are later.
later_sites.unpinnedWhy: Not a pin on the painted West Point face (TOWN_HOTSPOTS has no wp_sandy_gulch). It is also not in this camp: OHP No. 253 puts the monument 2.1 mi down Hwy 26 toward Glencoe, so it is shown on the horizon by bearing, never on a camp tile.
